regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Adenocarcinoma NSCLC · phase must be selected
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Docetaxel prevents normal rearrangement of the cell structures needed for division. It affects cancer cells and can also suppress blood cells, irritate nerves and cause fluid retention. Nintedanib blocks several signals involved in the growth of blood vessels that support a tumour. Its effects can also cause diarrhoea, liver changes, bleeding and wound-healing problems.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adenocarcinoma NSCLC · phase must be selected
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Docetaxel: Stabilises microtubules. Nintedanib: Blocks VEGF, FGF and PDGF receptor signalling.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Day 1: docetaxel drip, with no nintedanib. Days 2–21: nintedanib capsules twice daily. Repeat every 21 days for up to 6 cycles (about 18 weeks without delays); treatment may stop earlier. A later tablet-only phase needs a new team-confirmed plan.
key_points: Adenocarcinoma after first-line chemotherapy; ECOG 0–1 and life expectancy>3 months; more than one prior advanced-disease chemotherapy regimen excluded.
Combination docetaxel 75 mg/m² Day 1 / nintedanib 200 mgBD Days 2–21 up to 6 cycles. No nintedanib on docetaxel day.
At least 4 completed combination cycles before consultant-authorised nintedanib-only continuation, then continuous dosing in 28-day cycles.
Nintedanib liver, GI and dose-level actions differ from docetaxel neutropenia/skin/neuropathy/stomatitis actions.

Nintedanib liver interruption thresholds use bilirubin in combination with transaminases or transaminases>5; the old generic>3 rule was incorrect.

Give an early diarrhoea action plan with oral hydration and prescribed anti-diarrhoeal treatment; ongoing/severe symptoms need assessment and possible interruption.
Nintedanib is not taken on docetaxel Day 1. No double dose after a missed capsule.
Review P-gp interactions, liver tests, BP, bleeding, renal status, surgery/wound healing and contraception.

longitudinal_schedule.title: My treatment and safety checks

rows.label: Kidneys / liver / BP
cells: BP as indicated; extra tests if needed

longitudinal_schedule.note: Routine safety tests are separate from scans and tumour markers, which follow your individual plan. No universal imaging or tumour-marker interval is specified.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1: docetaxel drip, with no nintedanib. Days 2–21: nintedanib capsules twice daily. Repeat every 21 days for up to 6 cycles (about 18 weeks without delays); treatment may stop earlier. A later tablet-only phase needs a new team-confirmed plan.
route_and_duration: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² is infused over 60 minutes on Day 1. Nintedanib starting dose is 200 mg per dose twice daily on Days 2–21, about 12 hours apart with food. Use the actual prescribed capsule strength after any reduction; never take nintedanib on the docetaxel day.
practical_workflow: Take the prescribed steroid course from the day before docetaxel. If missed, contact the unit before attending; do not invent a catch-up dose.
The team should consider preventive G-CSF injections and arrange blood counts around the low-count period. Fever needs immediate advice.
Take nintedanib about 12 hours apart with food; swallow whole. Do not open, chew or crush. If missed, take the next scheduled dose only; never double up.
Have the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal and fluid plan ready. Contact oncology early for diarrhoea, poor intake or vomiting; do not wait 7 days to seek help.
Check all medicines and supplements with oncology/pharmacy. Nintedanib has P-gp interactions; docetaxel has CYP 3 A interactions, including grapefruit concerns.

Discuss fertility and effective contraception. Nintedanib requires contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after; follow the longest advice for your complete regimen. Vomiting/diarrhoea can reduce pill absorption.
observation_and_access: Appropriate IV access and reaction-management facilities for infused treatment; oral dispensing and handling review for capsules.

regimen_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 1314 adults with stageIIIB/IV recurrent NSCLC after first-line chemotherapy; prespecified adenocarcinoma subgroup 658 patients.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² Day 1 plus nintedanib 200 mg twice daily Days 2–21 versus docetaxel plus placebo.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: The licensed/NCCP population is adenocarcinoma after first-line chemotherapy. Overall-population PFS and adenocarcinoma-subgroup OS are labelled separately; this does not establish an independent benefit from maintenance-only initiation.

endpoints.interpretation: Primary intention-to-treat endpoint, not adenocarcinoma-only PFS.
Prespecified stepwise subgroup analysis; overall trial population OS was not significantly improved.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: The trial found a progression-free benefit overall and an overall-survival benefit in the prespecified adenocarcinoma subgroup.
limitations: Historical second-line trial after chemotherapy; applicability after contemporary chemo-immunotherapy requires consultant judgement.
Continuation is linked to prior combination treatment; the trial is not evidence for starting nintedanib alone.
harms: Grade≥3 diarrhoea and liver-enzyme elevations were more frequent with nintedanib; neutropenic infection requires prevention and monitoring.

evidence_audit.status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
indications_reviewed: NCCP 00372 a: locally advanced, metastatic stageIIIB/IV or locally recurrent adenocarcinoma NSCLC after first-line chemotherapy.
remaining_uncertainties: Adenocarcinoma after first-line chemotherapy; ECOG 0–1 and life expectancy>3 months; more than one prior advanced-disease chemotherapy regimen excluded.
Combination docetaxel 75 mg/m² Day 1 / nintedanib 200 mgBD Days 2–21 up to 6 cycles. No nintedanib on docetaxel day.
At least 4 completed combination cycles before consultant-authorised nintedanib-only continuation, then continuous dosing in 28-day cycles.
Nintedanib liver, GI and dose-level actions differ from docetaxel neutropenia/skin/neuropathy/stomatitis actions.
Source gaps: CrCl exactly 30; ANC exactly 1.5; docetaxel hepatic-table AND/OR layout. These require explicit specialist reconciliation.
Nintedanib liver interruption thresholds use bilirubin in combination with transaminases or transaminases>5; the old generic>3 rule was incorrect.

drug_profiles.name: Cisplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with cell copying. Fluids and kidney checks help reduce harm to healthy tissue.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Etoposide
drug_profiles.mechanism: Etoposide blocks an enzyme cells need while copying DNA. The route and prescribed amount differ between infusion and capsules; they are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Paclitaxel stabilises structures needed for cell division. It can also affect nerves, blood cells and healthy tissues. Premedicines help reduce infusion reactions.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with cell copying. Its dose uses kidney filtration and target exposure(AUC), not a fixed number of milligrams.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Chest radiotherapy
drug_profiles.mechanism: Radiotherapy directs radiation at the planned chest area. Its appointments and dose are set by the radiation oncology team.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Bevacizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps new blood vessels grow. It can slow tumour growth but also affect normal blood vessels and wound healing.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Docetaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Docetaxel prevents normal rearrangement of the cell structures needed for division. It affects cancer cells and can also suppress blood cells, irritate nerves and cause fluid retention.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Nintedanib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Nintedanib blocks several signals involved in the growth of blood vessels that support a tumour. Its effects can also cause diarrhoea, liver changes, bleeding and wound-healing problems.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
